title: register-correct prior, driven (telegraphic/coordinate): unicity + search + LLM judge
hypothesis: K4's plaintext is terse telegraphic/coordinate text recoverable under a register-matched prior that the prose prior buried
best_partial: D_tele=4.0 (crossover k=5); register judge calibrated=True (reg 97.5/gib 0); candidate max 75
insights: (A) REGISTER UNICITY: telegraphic entropy rate r=0.702 -> D_tele=3.998 bits/char (prose D=3.62). Hand-crafted under-determination gap by k: [(1, -290.9), (2, -213.2), (3, -128.4), (4, -41.6), (5, 41.5), (6, 133.7)]; register crossover k=5 (prose was k=5). Telegraphic text is MORE redundant (formulaic) than prose -> unicity is BETTER; fewer register decryptions are consistent, so the register prior could narrow the solution set.

(B) REGISTER-DRIVEN SEARCH: maximised a telegraphic char-LM over the 73 free positions; 0/28 distinct candidates reach the 5th-pct bar -0.623. CAVEAT: the synthetic register corpus is pathologically formulaic (repeated DEGREES/MINUTES/NORTH), so its char-LM bar is unreachable by natural text -- this part is mis-calibrated and uninformative; the LLM judge (C) is the meaningful register test. Top register candidate: YLATYMIYEGHNIROATELAYEASTNORTHEASTONDINGFORTFIIEDMIH...

(C) REGISTER LLM JUDGE (gemma4:31b-it-q8_0): calibration reg-ctrl 97.5 / gibberish 0 / prose 3.3 (prose scores LOW under the navigational prompt, as expected) -> trustworthy=True. Register candidates: max 75 (vs the PROSE-judge max of 10 in exp 095). Best: FDUTMDYDEPMIRTFIVEDBEEASTNORTHEASTDTENDEGREEFIVN

NUANCE, not a solve: crib-consistent decryptions wear a COORDINATE COSTUME far better than a prose one (judge max 75 here vs 10 in 095) -- weak support that K4's register is telegraphic. BUT this is partly CIRCULAR (the search maximises register-ness, then a register-tuned judge measures it) and the best candidate is coordinate-FLAVOURED SALAD ('FIVE...TEN DEGREE...EASTNORTHEAST' fragments amid gibberish), below the 97.5 control bar and non-unique. So the register prior is PLAUSIBLE but does NOT break the under-determination: many coordinate-flavoured crib-consistent decryptions exist, none a coherent unique message. The mis-specified-prior idea is addressed (register is apt) but insufficient -- it does not single out the plaintext.
next_steps: register reframing is plausible (decryptions wear a coordinate costume far better than prose: judge 75 vs 10) but partly circular and still under-determined -- it does not single out the plaintext. Remaining open: partial/consensus determination (exp 098) and the interruptor keystream (exp 099)
